\section[el localizador]{el localizador — the booking reference}

\label{lesson:ES-C662-localizador}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for the stay, then the Spanish for the concierge.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: el localizador}
\textbf{el localizador} — \textquotedblleft{}the booking reference\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Dígame el localizador de su billete, por favor.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Tell me the booking reference for your ticket, please.}
\end{quote}

A short code of letters and numbers.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{localizador} is built on \emph{localizar} \textquotedblleft{}to locate\textquotedblright{}, from \emph{local}, a learned borrowing from Late Latin \emph{locālis} (EtymDB), from \emph{locus} \textquotedblleft{}place\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{el localizador}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{el localizador}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{el localizador}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Spanish for the stay, then the Spanish for the concierge, then say \emph{el localizador} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\section[modificar]{modificar — to change, to modify}

\label{lesson:ES-C662-modificar}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for the concierge, then the Spanish for the booking reference.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: modificar}
\textbf{modificar} — \textquotedblleft{}to change, to modify\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
¿Puedo modificar la fecha de la reserva?
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Can I change the date of the booking?}
\end{quote}

The c becomes qu before e: \emph{modifiqué}. Formal, common on booking sites.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{modificar} is a learned borrowing from Latin \emph{modificāre} \textquotedblleft{}to set limits to, to regulate\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short; EtymDB), built from \emph{modus} \textquotedblleft{}measure\textquotedblright{} and \emph{facere} \textquotedblleft{}to make\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{modificar}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{modificar}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{modificar}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Spanish for the concierge, then the Spanish for the booking reference, then say \emph{modificar} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\section[la confirmación]{la confirmación — the confirmation}

\label{lesson:ES-C662-confirmacion}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for the booking reference, then the Spanish for to change.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: la confirmación}
\textbf{la confirmación} — \textquotedblleft{}the confirmation\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Recibí la confirmación del vuelo.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{I got the flight confirmation.}
\end{quote}

It is also a church ceremony.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{confirmación} is a learned borrowing from Latin \emph{cōnfirmātiō} (EtymDB), from \emph{cōnfirmāre} \textquotedblleft{}to make firm\textquotedblright{}, built on \emph{firmus} \textquotedblleft{}firm\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[la penalización]{la penalización — the penalty, the charge (for cancelling)}

\label{lesson:ES-C662-penalizacion}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for to change, then the Spanish for the confirmation.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: la penalización}
\textbf{la penalización} — \textquotedblleft{}the penalty, the charge (for cancelling)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Si cancela hoy, no hay penalización.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{If you cancel today, there is no charge.}
\end{quote}

Booking terms often say \emph{sin penalización} — free of charge.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{penalización} is built on \emph{penalizar} \textquotedblleft{}to penalise\textquotedblright{}, from \emph{penal}, a learned borrowing from Latin \emph{poenālis}, built on \emph{poena} \textquotedblleft{}penalty, punishment\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[la cancelación]{la cancelación — the cancellation}

\label{lesson:ES-C662-cancelacion}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for the confirmation, then the Spanish for the penalty.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: la cancelación}
\textbf{la cancelación} — \textquotedblleft{}the cancellation\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
La cancelación es gratis hasta el viernes.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Cancellation is free until Friday.}
\end{quote}

\emph{Un seguro de cancelación} — cancellation insurance.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{cancelación} is built on \emph{cancelar}, a learned borrowing from Latin \emph{cancellāre} \textquotedblleft{}to cross out with lines like a lattice\textquotedblright{}, from \emph{cancellī} \textquotedblleft{}bars\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}
